newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Jan trade surplus fits year fcast - Galland.
newsitem.headline: French Jan trade surplus fits year fcast - Galland.

text.p: French Foreign trade minister Yves Galland said on Friday that the country's January trade surplus fitted with a forecast of a trade surplus well over 100 billion francs in 1997 excluding trade with overseas departments.
The customs office said on Friday the January trade surplus was 11.723 billion francs.
Back in February, Galland had also forecast a trade surplus in 1997 of 135-145 billion francs -- including DOM trade.

The provisional January figure announced on Friday stripped out trade between mainland France and its overseas departments (DOMs) and would have been 14 billion francs if DOM trade had been included, Galland said in a statement.
It was the first time the headline figure from the customs office excluded trade with the overseas territories, he said.
The December customs office figure was revised, stripping out the DOM trade initially included and bringing the surplus down to 8.528 billion francs from 11.328 billion.
France's 1996 trade surplus was initially reported at a record of 122.340 billion francs unadjusted.
But this was restated in the Friday announcement at 93.076 billion francs, versus a comparable 1995 unadjusted surplus of 67.186 billion.
